How does this API comparison work?

This page compares pay-as-you-go API rates for the same model, at the same resolution when the vendor stated it. Catalog rows are used where they exist. WaveSpeed and Runware are not in the catalog, so their figures were read from official pages today and are labelled as such. A sale rate is shown next to its list rate and end date. Token-billed or estimated rows stay labelled as estimates. Variants with different names, such as MiniMax H3 and MiniMax H3 Max Turbo, are not treated as one price.

    Replicate is best for Wan 3.0 at 480p and for Seedance 2.5 at 480p with no video input, among the catalog rows we can compare, and those Replicate rates were also on the vendor pages today. Runware’s Wan 3.0 sale is best for the lowest verified 480p Wan 3.0 API rate we could read today, through November 23, 2026. It is not for a post-sale rate below fal, because the published list then matches fal. fal remains a useful default when you already use its endpoint, but it is not the cheapest verified option for those two models.     How do we calculate this?

    Each dollar figure is a current price row, with the vendor page and the date that page was checked. A published rate is a dollars-per-second figure on that page, or an API credit count times the credit price the page states. A credit-plan figure is plan price ÷ credits × credits per clip ÷ seconds, and it assumes every credit you pay for is used. When the vendor marks that count with "~", "roughly", or "estimated", the row is labelled estimated from credit plan and is not a list price. A promo shows its end date when the vendor gave one. The full method is on the about page (https://vidfare.com/about/).
